plan: [Third-price auction (3 bidders): if I win I pay the lowest other bid, so my bid mainly controls winning. With no history and independent draws, bidding my true value ($25) is a robust, long-run-safe choice: I win when the opponents' minimum bid is below 25 and earn positive surplus, while avoiding systematic overpayment when opponent lows exceed my value.]

[Bid my true value ($17). In a 3-bidder third-price auction the winner pays the lowest bid; bidding my value guarantees that if I win both others bid less than $17, so payment < value and profit ≥ 0. Overbidding risks winning when the minimum exceeds $17, causing losses; underbidding misses profitable wins. Truthful bidding maximizes expected long-run profit given independent draws.]

[Given my value v=39 and opponents' values iid Uniform[0,49], bidding higher raises win probability while the price I pay (the third-highest = the minimum of the other two bids) stays driven by opponents. Approximating opponents as bidding their values, expected utility ≈ (b/49)^2*(39 - b/3), which increases on [0,49]. Thus I will bid the maximum allowed, 49, to maximize expected profit; there is a small chance both opponents exceed 39 and I lose money, but expected gain is maximized at 49.]
